audit_status.source_base: Greek James text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact draft reviewed for trials/testing, wisdom, double-mindedness, rich/poor reversal, desire/sin/death chain, implanted word, doers, pure religion.

verses.restored: James, servant of Divine and of Lord Jesus Messiah, to the twelve tribes in the dispersion: rejoice.

familiar.text: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.

modern.text: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, To the twelve tribes of the Dispersion: Greetings. Rejoicing in Trials (Philippians 1:12–20)

original.text: Ἰάκωβος θεοῦ καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ δοῦλος ταῖς δώδεκα φυλαῖς ταῖς ἐν τῇ διασπορᾷ χαίρειν.

verses.restored: Count it all joy, my siblings, whenever you fall into various tests/trials,

familiar.text: My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations;

modern.text: Consider it pure joy, my brothers, when you encounter trials of many kinds,

original.text: Πᾶσαν χαρὰν ἡγήσασθε, ἀδελφοί μου, ὅταν πειρασμοῖς περιπέσητε ποικίλοις,

verses.restored: knowing that the testing of your trust produces endurance.

familiar.text: Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience.

modern.text: because you know that the testing of your faith develops perseverance.

original.text: γινώσκοντες ὅτι τὸ δοκίμιον ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως κατεργάζεται ὑπομονήν·

verses.restored: And let endurance have complete work, so that you may be complete and whole, lacking in nothing.

familiar.text: But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.

modern.text: Allow perseverance to finish its work, so that you may be mature and complete, not lacking anything.

original.text: ἡ δὲ ὑπομονὴ ἔργον τέλειον ἐχέτω, ἵνα ἦτε τέλειοι καὶ ὁλόκληροι, ἐν μηδενὶ λειπόμενοι.

verses.restored: But if any of you lacks wisdom, let one ask from the Divine, who gives to all generously and without reproach, and it will be given.

familiar.text: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.

modern.text: Now if any of you lacks wisdom, he should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault, and it will be given to him.

original.text: Εἰ δέ τις ὑμῶν λείπεται σοφίας, αἰτείτω παρὰ τοῦ διδόντος θεοῦ πᾶσιν ἁπλῶς καὶ ⸀μὴ ὀνειδίζοντος, καὶ δοθήσεται αὐτῷ·

verses.restored: But let one ask in trust, doubting nothing, for the doubting one is like a wave of sea driven and tossed by wind.

familiar.text: But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.

modern.text: But he must ask in faith, without doubting, because he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, blown and tossed by the wind.

original.text: αἰτείτω δὲ ἐν πίστει, μηδὲν διακρινόμενος, ὁ γὰρ διακρινόμενος ἔοικεν κλύδωνι θαλάσσης ἀνεμιζομένῳ καὶ ῥιπιζομένῳ·

verses.restored: For let not that human suppose that one will receive anything from the Lord,

familiar.text: For let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord.

modern.text: That man should not expect to receive anything from the Lord.

original.text: μὴ γὰρ οἰέσθω ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὅτι λήμψεταί τι παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου

verses.restored: a double-souled human, unstable in all one's ways.

familiar.text: A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.

modern.text: He is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.

original.text: ἀνὴρ δίψυχος, ἀκατάστατος ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Let the lowly sibling boast in one's height,

familiar.text: Let the brother of low degree rejoice in that he is exalted:

modern.text: The brother in humble circumstances should exult in his high position.

original.text: Καυχάσθω δὲ ὁ ἀδελφὸς ὁ ταπεινὸς ἐν τῷ ὕψει αὐτοῦ,

verses.restored: and the rich one in one's lowliness, because like flower of grass one will pass away.

familiar.text: But the rich, in that he is made low: because as the flower of the grass he shall pass away.

modern.text: But the one who is rich should exult in his low position, because he will pass away like a flower of the field.

original.text: ὁ δὲ πλούσιος ἐν τῇ ταπεινώσει αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ὡς ἄνθος χόρτου παρελεύσεται.

verses.restored: For the sun rises with scorching heat and dries the grass, and its flower falls, and the beauty of its face perishes; so also the rich one will fade in one's journeys.

familiar.text: For the sun is no sooner risen with a burning heat, but it withereth the grass, and the flower thereof falleth, and the grace of the fashion of it perisheth: so also shall the rich man fade away in his ways.

modern.text: For the sun rises with scorching heat and withers the plant; its flower falls and its beauty is lost. So too, the rich man will fade away in the midst of his pursuits.

original.text: ἀνέτειλεν γὰρ ὁ ἥλιος σὺν τῷ καύσωνι καὶ ἐξήρανεν τὸν χόρτον, καὶ τὸ ἄνθος αὐτοῦ ἐξέπεσεν καὶ ἡ εὐπρέπεια τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ ἀπώλετο· οὕτως καὶ ὁ πλούσιος ἐν ταῖς πορείαις αὐτοῦ μαρανθήσεται.

verses.restored: Blessed is the human who endures testing, because having become approved, one will receive the crown of life that he promised to those loving him.

familiar.text: Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.

modern.text: Blessed is the man who perseveres under trial, because when he has stood the test, he will receive the crown of life that God has promised to those who love Him. Good and Perfect Gifts

original.text: Μακάριος ἀνὴρ ὃς ὑπομένει πειρασμόν, ὅτι δόκιμος γενόμενος λήμψεται τὸν στέφανον τῆς ζωῆς, ὃν ⸀ἐπηγγείλατο τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Let no one being tested say, I am tested by the Divine; for the Divine is untested by harmful things and tests no one with harm.

familiar.text: Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man:

modern.text: When tempted, no one should say, “God is tempting me.” For God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does He tempt anyone.

original.text: μηδεὶς πειραζόμενος λεγέτω ὅτι Ἀπὸ θεοῦ πειράζομαι· ὁ γὰρ θεὸς ἀπείραστός ἐστιν κακῶν, πειράζει δὲ αὐτὸς οὐδένα.

verses.restored: But each one is tested by one's own desire, being drawn out and enticed.

familiar.text: But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.

modern.text: But each one is tempted when by his own evil desires he is lured away and enticed.

original.text: ἕκαστος δὲ πειράζεται ὑπὸ τῆς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας ἐξελκόμενος καὶ δελεαζόμενος·

verses.restored: Then desire, having conceived, gives birth to sin/misalignment; and sin/misalignment, having been completed, brings forth death.

familiar.text: Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.

modern.text: Then after desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death.

original.text: εἶτα ἡ ἐπιθυμία συλλαβοῦσα τίκτει ἁμαρτίαν, ἡ δὲ ἁμαρτία ἀποτελεσθεῖσα ἀποκύει θάνατον.

verses.restored: Do not be deceived, my beloved siblings.

familiar.text: Do not err, my beloved brethren.

modern.text: Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers.

original.text: μὴ πλανᾶσθε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί.

verses.restored: Every good giving and every complete gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow of turning.

familiar.text: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.

modern.text: Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights, with whom there is no change or shifting shadow.

original.text: Πᾶσα δόσις ἀγαθὴ καὶ πᾶν δώρημα τέλειον ἄνωθέν ἐστιν, καταβαῖνον ἀπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς τῶν φώτων, παρʼ ᾧ οὐκ ἔνι παραλλαγὴ ἢ τροπῆς ἀποσκίασμα.

verses.restored: Having willed, he gave us birth by word of truth, so that we might be a kind of firstfruit of his creatures.

familiar.text: Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.

modern.text: He chose to give us birth through the word of truth, that we would be a kind of firstfruits of His creation. Hearing and Doing

original.text: βουληθεὶς ἀπεκύησεν ἡμᾶς λόγῳ ἀληθείας, εἰς τὸ εἶναι ἡμᾶς ἀπαρχήν τινα τῶν αὐτοῦ κτισμάτων.

verses.restored: Know this, my beloved siblings: let every human be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger,

familiar.text: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:

modern.text: My beloved brothers, understand this: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger,

original.text: ⸀Ἴστε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί. ἔστω ⸀δὲ πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ταχὺς εἰς τὸ ἀκοῦσαι, βραδὺς εἰς τὸ λαλῆσαι, βραδὺς εἰς ὀργήν,

verses.restored: for human anger does not produce the righteousness/justice of the Divine.

familiar.text: For the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God.

modern.text: for man’s anger does not bring about the righteousness that God desires.

original.text: ὀργὴ γὰρ ἀνδρὸς δικαιοσύνην θεοῦ ⸂οὐκ ἐργάζεται⸃.

verses.restored: Therefore putting away all filth and overflow of harmfulness, receive in gentleness the implanted word able to save/heal your souls/lives.

familiar.text: Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness, and receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.

modern.text: Therefore, get rid of all moral filth and every expression of evil, and humbly accept the word planted in you, which can save your souls.

original.text: διὸ ἀποθέμενοι πᾶσαν ῥυπαρίαν καὶ περισσείαν κακίας ἐν πραΰτητι δέξασθε τὸν ἔμφυτον λόγον τὸν δυνάμενον σῶσαι τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν.

verses.restored: But become doers of word, and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves.

familiar.text: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.

modern.text: Be doers of the word, and not hearers only. Otherwise, you are deceiving yourselves.

original.text: Γίνεσθε δὲ ποιηταὶ λόγου καὶ μὴ ⸂ἀκροαταὶ μόνον⸃ παραλογιζόμενοι ἑαυτούς.

verses.restored: For if anyone is hearer of word and not doer, this one is like a human observing the face of one's birth in a mirror.

familiar.text: For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass:

modern.text: For anyone who hears the word but does not carry it out is like a man who looks at his face in a mirror,

original.text: ὅτι εἴ τις ἀκροατὴς λόγου ἐστὶν καὶ οὐ ποιητής, οὗτος ἔοικεν ἀνδρὶ κατανοοῦντι τὸ πρόσωπον τῆς γενέσεως αὐτοῦ ἐν ἐσόπτρῳ,

verses.restored: For one observes oneself and goes away and immediately forgets what sort one was.

familiar.text: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.

modern.text: and after observing himself goes away and immediately forgets what he looks like.

original.text: κατενόησεν γὰρ ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀπελήλυθεν καὶ εὐθέως ἐπελάθετο ὁποῖος ἦν.

verses.restored: But the one looking into complete Law, the Law of freedom, and remaining, not becoming forgetful hearer but doer of work, this one will be blessed in one's doing.

familiar.text: But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.

modern.text: But the one who looks intently into the perfect law of freedom, and continues to do so—not being a forgetful hearer, but an effective doer—he will be blessed in what he does.

original.text: ὁ δὲ παρακύψας εἰς νόμον τέλειον τὸν τῆς ἐλευθερίας καὶ παραμείνας, ⸀οὐκ ἀκροατὴς ἐπιλησμονῆς γενόμενος ἀλλὰ ποιητὴς ἔργου, οὗτος μακάριος ἐν τῇ ποιήσει αὐτοῦ ἔσται.

verses.restored: If anyone thinks oneself reverent while not bridling one's tongue but deceiving one's heart, this one's reverence is empty.

familiar.text: If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue, but deceiveth his own heart, this man’s religion is vain.

modern.text: If anyone considers himself religious and yet does not bridle his tongue, he deceives his heart and his religion is worthless.

original.text: Εἴ τις δοκεῖ θρησκὸς ⸀εἶναι μὴ χαλιναγωγῶν γλῶσσαν ⸀αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ ἀπατῶν καρδίαν ⸀αὐτοῦ, τούτου μάταιος ἡ θρησκεία.

verses.restored: Pure and undefiled reverence before the Divine and Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their pressure, and to keep oneself unstained from the world.

familiar.text: Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.

modern.text: Pure and undefiled religion before our God and Father is this: to care for orphans and widows in their distress, and to keep oneself from being polluted by the world.

original.text: θρησκεία καθαρὰ καὶ ἀμίαντος παρὰ ⸀τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρὶ αὕτη ἐστίν, ἐπισκέπτεσθαι ὀρφανοὺς καὶ χήρας ἐν τῇ θλίψει αὐτῶν, ἄσπιλον ἑαυτὸν τηρεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ κόσμου.

translation_notes: James is wisdom-parenesis: tests produce endurance but suffering is not romanticized.
Human anger does not produce Divine justice.
Pure religion is concrete care for vulnerable people plus integrity, not ritual performance alone.
